![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14096165/assets/89fa15ffb9a7f6b319cf3b9ff0de4ab821a15f632d7f93618fbe99b7979260f4.png)

Describe the set of points shown above using set-builder notation.
e-13145.worked_solution:
Since all points $P(x,y)$ in our set lie at integer values of $x$ and $y,$ we have $x\in \mathbb Z, y\in\mathbb Z,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in \mathbb Z\times\mathbb Z = \mathbb Z^2.
$$

The points $P(x,y)$ satisfy the condition

$$
x \in \{1,2,3\}, \quad y \in \{ -3,-2,-1,0,1,2 \}.
$$

In other words,

$$
1 \leq x \leq 3, \quad -3 \leq y \leq 2
$$

Therefore, we can write our set as follows:

$$
\Big\{ (x,y)  \in \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\mathbb Z^2}
\: : \: 
\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}1}  
\leq  x \leq  
\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}3} , \: 
\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}-3}  
\leq  y \leq  
\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}2} 
\Big\}.
$$

after.worked_solution:
A point $P(x,y)$ lies inside the rectangle if the following conditions are satisfied:

$$
\begin{aligned}2<x<6,\,2<y<5\end{aligned}
$$

Moreover, since *every* real value in these intervals is included, $x\in R,y\in R,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in R\times R={R}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we can write our set as follows:

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,2<x<6,\,\,2<y<5}
$$

content.worked_solution:
A point $P(x,y)$ lies inside the rectangle if the following conditions are satisfied:

$$
\begin{aligned}2<x<6,\,2<y<5\end{aligned}
$$

Moreover, since *every* real value in these intervals is included, $x\in R,y\in R,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in R\times R={R}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we can write our set as follows:

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,2<x<6,\,\,2<y<5}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Since all points $P(x,y)$ in our set lie at integer values of $x$ and $y,$ we have $x\in Z,y\in Z,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in Z\times Z={Z}^{2}.
$$

The points $P(x,y)$ satisfy the condition

$$
x\in {-1,0,1,2},\,y\in {-2,-1,0,1,2,3}.
$$

In other words,

$$
-1\le x\le 2,\,-2\le y\le 3.
$$

Therefore, we can write our set as follows:

$$

content.worked_solution:
Since all points $P(x,y)$ in our set lie at integer values of $x$ and $y,$ we have $x\in Z,y\in Z,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in Z\times Z={Z}^{2}.
$$

The points $P(x,y)$ satisfy the condition

$$
x\in {-1,0,1,2},\,y\in {-2,-1,0,1,2,3}.
$$

In other words,

$$
-1\le x\le 2,\,-2\le y\le 3.
$$

Therefore, we can write our set as follows:

$$
{(x,y)\in {Z}^{2}\,:\,-1\le x\le 2,\,-2\le y\le 3}
$$

after.worked_solution:
A point $P(x,y)$ lies *inside* the rectangle if the following conditions are satisfied:

$$
\begin{aligned}3<x<6,\,-1<y<4\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we also need to *include* the left edge ($x=3$).

Therefore, we change the corresponding inequality symbol to non-strict, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\le x<6,\,-1<y<4\end{aligned}
$$

Moreover, since *every* real value in these intervals is included, $x\in R,y\in R,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in R\times R={R}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we can write our set as follows:

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,3\le x<6,\,-1<y<4}
$$

after.worked_solution:
A point $P(x,y)$ lies inside or on the rectangle's edges if the following conditions are satisfied:

$$
\begin{aligned}1\le x\le 6,\,3\le y\le 5\end{aligned}
$$

Moreover, since *every* real value in these intervals is included, $x\in R,y\in R,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in R\times R={R}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we can write our set as follows:

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,1\le x\le 6,\,3\le y\le 5}
$$

content.worked_solution:
A point $P(x,y)$ lies inside or on the rectangle's edges if the following conditions are satisfied:

$$
\begin{aligned}1\le x\le 6,\,3\le y\le 5\end{aligned}
$$

Moreover, since *every* real value in these intervals is included, $x\in R,y\in R,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in R\times R={R}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we can write our set as follows:

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,1\le x\le 6,\,3\le y\le 5}
$$
